title: "Reproduce Image-in-Div Bug"
author: "Tester"
format:
  revealjs:
    slide-number: true
---

:::{.qrcodeblock}

Oh hello

![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/a/a9/Example.jpg)

:::

:::

## Slide C: outer div + inner div

:::: {.anotherblocks}

1.explanation:
1. Save the above as `test-div-image-bug.qmd`.
2. Run `quarto preview test-div-image-bug.qmd` (or `quarto render --to revealjs test-div-image-bug.qmd`).
3. Navigate to Slides A, B, and C.  

You will observe:
- Slide A (.qrcodeblock) and Slide C (.anotherblocks → .qrcodeblockagain) show the image _after_ the closing div rather than between the two lines of text.
- Slide B (using `.columns`/`.column`) correctly places the image inline.

This minimal file reproduces the placement bug for images inside arbitrary div blocks in a Reveal.js presentation built with Quarto.
1.bug_scenario: On slides using a custom Markdown block (e.g. ::: {.qrcodeblock}) or an outer arbitrary div (:::: {.anotherblocks}), any inline image you drop into the block is rendered _after_ the block rather than between the preceding and following text. In other words, “Oh hello” and “Why not?” stay inside the block but the image is bumped outside. However, if you nest the image inside a {.columns}/{.column} structure, it stays in-place.
